object_description: simple school volume with split levels, loggias and a conventional attic
design_condition: The building forms a new address toward the street while opening generous and connected outdoor spaces, but its proximity to the existing school and detached kindergarten remain problematic.

positive.statement: The simple and coherent urban development creates a permeable outdoor space between the building islands.
The new open space and all-weather pitch establish a clear new school address.
The connection to the existing path system improves access.
The flowing green space becomes a coherent unit through careful tree planting.
The functions are arranged clearly, with catering toward the primary school and care facilities toward the street.
The classrooms are easily divided into the respective cluster units using the two access cores.
The two-story loggias illuminate the deep floor plans and create an inspiring place for teaching.
The industrial expression is logically continued in the structural design inside.
The project impresses with a harmonious situation, precise open-space interventions and a clear arrangement of functions.

negative.statement: The proximity of the new building to the existing primary school buildings appears critical.
The eastern outbuilding raises questions in terms of urban planning.
The garage exit obscures the basic volumetric disposition and the addressing of the school.
The entrance and transition to the stairwells are not convincing and prevent natural access to the rooms.
The conventional attic floor is questioned for a public building.
The purpose of the skylights in the playground area is questioned.
The basement kitchen has little natural light and is unsuitable as a full-fledged workspace.
The exterior expression is less convincing in relation to the existing school and the district.
The spatial structure and internal sequence of room sequences appear somewhat functional in certain areas.
